directive: **UI** — runs AFTER Features: turn the defined features into a **live, navigable UI the user can explore**, generated IN-APP by the designer — not sent out to an external tool (#3783). Once the screens are mapped, **commission the internal designer to build the UI shell**: hand it a page-per-screen spec over `bsc-commission designer` and let it author the screens from the shared component kit **reuse-first** — check `bsc ui list` and prefer existing components; where a screen needs something the kit lacks, commission a **general, always-applicable** component (never a one-off) so the kit grows coherently. The delivered pages render live in the planner's **preview pane**, assembled into a navigable shell the user clicks through screen to screen. Choose each screen's layout by its data's SHAPE: **if the project has a Data Model** (`bsc data model get` — non-null once a migration/data project inferred one), DERIVE THE SHAPE MECHANICALLY rather than by eye — `bsc data shapes` returns, per entity, RANKED candidates (`list` · `linked-list` · `tree` · `graph` · `table` · `key-value` · `series`) each with a confidence and the structural reason it fired (a self-referencing ref → tree, a next/prev link or sequence column → linked-list, a join table → graph, a name+value pair → key-value, a temporal axis + a numeric measure → series, otherwise table/list by column density). Lead with the top candidate, but where two tie (a lone self-reference is a tree ONLY if an item has one parent) ASK the user — the schema cannot settle it. Name each screen's chosen shape so the designer picks the matching kit components, and fold the **Platform Behavior Summary** (`bsc data scan get` — validation rules, Flows/Process Builder, approval processes captured in the Source scan) into the screens' states/flows + validation — so the UI is data-driven over the real schema, not generic. Write `ui.md` with the screen inventory. You author no UI code yourself — you spec, and the designer builds. **Fallback (external design):** if the user would rather design externally, author a Claude Design kickoff at `prompts/ui-kickoff.md` and route any files they drop under `design/` (check `design/intake.json`, the file-intake manifest) into the UI repo (e.g. `<repo>/src/components/`), referenced in the UI stream's worker kickoff — the same routing clears the stage.
name: UI

require.label: route the design to the project

blurb: Screens and flows from the features — the designer builds a live, navigable UI shell in-app (reuse-first), previewed as you plan; external design optional.
prompt:
With the features defined, turn them into a **live, navigable UI** generated in-app — do not send the
user out to an external tool. Read the features and map the screens each one needs, then
**commission the internal designer to build the UI shell**: hand it a page-per-screen spec over
`bsc-commission designer` and let it author each screen from the shared component kit **reuse-first** —
run `bsc ui list`, prefer an existing component, and only when a screen needs something the kit lacks
commission a **general, always-applicable** component (never a one-off). The delivered pages render
live in the preview pane as a navigable shell the user can click through. Write `ui.md` with the
screen inventory.

When the project has a Data Model, do not guess how each entity should be rendered: run
`bsc data shapes` (add an entity key for just one, `--pretty` for indented JSON). It infers each
entity's ideal DATA SHAPE from the model's own structure — self-referencing refs, chain links,
join tables, attribute bags, column density — and returns RANKED candidates with a confidence and
a reason, never a single guessed answer. Name the chosen shape per screen so the designer picks the
matching kit components; where the top two candidates are equally plausible, put the question to the
user rather than picking silently.

You author no UI code yourself — you spec, and the designer builds. **Fallback:** if the user prefers
to design externally, author a Claude Design kickoff at `prompts/ui-kickoff.md` and route any files
they drop under `design/` into the UI repo — the same routing clears the stage.

Gate: the UI shell is generated (or external design routed) to the project.
routePrompt: The user just added files under design/ — see design/intake.json for the manifest. For each staged file: examine it, classify it, and route it to the right place in this project. Use `bsc plan repo list` to pick the relevant repo (e.g. copy design assets into the repo that owns the UI), copy the file into that repo's directory, and reference it in the appropriate section file. In a multi-repo project, only attach UI assets to the UI-bearing repo. If a file's destination is ambiguous, ask me before placing it.
